slides.title: Meet Dot
slides.text: Dot the fox is a data detective. Dot solves cases with facts, not guesses.
slides.alt: Dot opens the first case: a table of lunchroom facts in rows and columns, with the case question at the top.

slides.title: Data is facts in rows
slides.text: A table holds facts in rows and columns. A table full of facts does not answer anything yet. You have to make the answer show.
slides.alt: Another case table: every row is one tower of blocks, every column one kind of fact about it.

slides.title: Sort or group
slides.text: Sorting puts the rows in order, like smallest to biggest. Grouping puts rows of the same kind together and counts them.
slides.alt: The pet case grouped: one bar per kind of pet, counted, so the most common pet jumps out of the chart.

slides.title: Who was in the lunchroom last?
slides.text: First find the rows for the place in the question. Then sort those rows by time: the last one is your answer.
slides.alt: The case sorted by time: the Hall rows now run in time order, so the last Hall row answers the question.

slides.title: Show me first
slides.text: Dot has one rule: you can only pin a claim when the view on the screen shows it. Most of each kind? Group and count.
slides.alt: With the grouped chart showing the evidence, the claim card opens: Dot will only pin a claim the view proves.

words.means: facts, like names, times and numbers
put rows in order by one column
put the same kinds together and count them

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Data Detective at Sort & Group and solve all 6 cases. For each one ask: which column is the question about?
slides.alt: Dot opens the first case: a table of lunchroom facts in rows and columns, with the case question at the top.
